brief:
Mohammad returned to his shelter at Abu Asi Orphan Camp in Al Bureij, central Gaza, in June 2025, hours after Israeli drones destroyed his vehicle moments after he left it, Dawn reported. He had been working to support displaced children and other Palestinians sheltering at the camp when the strike occurred.

Despite the narrow escape, Mohammad's sister Sara knew he would reject her pleas to rest and recover from the attack. The incident reflects the hazards confronting humanitarian workers operating amid Gaza's displacement camps, where thousands rely on aid deliveries and basic services provided by volunteers and relief organizations working in difficult conditions.
dek: When Mohammad returned to their shelter in the Abu Asi Orphan Camp in Al Bureij, central Gaza, in June 2025, Sara knew her brother would not listen to her plea for him to rest. Only hours earlier, Israeli drones had destroyed his vehicle just seconds after he had left it. His crime: Working to support children and other displaced Palestinians in the camp.
title: Israeli drones destroy Gaza aid worker's vehicle at orphan camp
